2
Which two units are identical when expressed in terms of SI base units?
A
J C–1 and kg m2
A–1
s–2
s–1
B
J s and kg m2
C
N m and kg m3
s–2
D
N s and kg m s–3

hints: Notice each option pairs a derived-unit product like $\text{J s}$ or $\text{N s}$ with a $\text{kg}$, $\text{m}$, $\text{s}$, $\text{A}$ combination - start by writing $1 \text{ J} = 1 \text{ N m}$ in base units.
Recall $1 \text{ N} = 1 \text{ kg m s}^{-2}$ from $F = ma$, and $1 \text{ C} = 1 \text{ A s}$, then expand the left-hand side of each pair.
Multiply or divide by the extra $\text{s}$, $\text{m}$ or $\text{C}^{-1}$ and check whether the powers of $\text{m}$ and $\text{s}$ match the right-hand side exactly.
walkthrough: Write the base units for force and energy: $1 \text{ N} = 1 \text{ kg m s}^{-2}$ and $1 \text{ J} = 1 \text{ N m} = 1 \text{ kg m}^2\text{s}^{-2}$.
Also recall charge in base units: $1 \text{ C} = 1 \text{ A s}$.
Test pair B: left side $1 \text{ J s} = (1 \text{ kg m}^2\text{s}^{-2})(1 \text{ s}) = 1 \text{ kg m}^2\text{s}^{-1}$.
This exactly equals the right side $\text{kg m}^2\text{s}^{-1}$, with matching powers of $\text{kg}$, $\text{m}$ and $\text{s}$.
The other pairs fail: $\text{J C}^{-1}$ gives $\text{kg m}^2\text{A}^{-1}\text{s}^{-3}$, $\text{N m}$ gives $\text{kg m}^2\text{s}^{-2}$, and $\text{N s}$ gives $\text{kg m s}^{-1}$.
Only the $\text{J s}$ pair is identical on both sides. This is option B.

A.explanation: $\text{J C}^{-1}$ is $\text{kg m}^2\text{s}^{-2}$ divided by $\text{A s}$, giving $\text{kg m}^2\text{A}^{-1}\text{s}^{-3}$, not $\text{kg m}^2\text{A}^{-1}\text{s}^{-2}$.

B.explanation: $\text{J s}$ is $(\text{kg m}^2\text{s}^{-2})(\text{s}) = \text{kg m}^2\text{s}^{-1}$, so both sides match exactly.

C.explanation: $\text{N m}$ is work with base units $\text{kg m}^2\text{s}^{-2}$, which has $\text{m}^2$ not $\text{m}^3$.

D.explanation: $\text{N s}$ is $(\text{kg m s}^{-2})(\text{s}) = \text{kg m s}^{-1}$, not $\text{kg m s}^{-3}$.
